correctness.rationale: The two-labeled original edges have a uniquely determined endpoint support C. Outside C, exactly binomial(n-|C|,2) pair-vertices are forced to label 1, while all other pair-vertices outside the chosen 2-set are optional 0/1. Labeled no-isolate support-graphs with k edges are counted exactly by A_{c,k} through inclusion-exclusion. This gives a disjoint exhaustive partition of all functions. The n-r endpoint coverage constraint gives 2k>=n-r and the sharp n-1 lower bound, with uniquely minimizing uncovered count 1 (odd n) or 2 (even n); equality forces a perfect matching and counts all optima. Checks: 49,660 direct ternary functions through n=5; 2^15 label-two support subsets at n=6 and all smaller n; min profiles through n=18. The proof, not finite tests, establishes the universal quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The claim n>=5 counts every weight of every Roman function on L(K_n), plus exact minimum-function types. Edge Roman domination on K_n is an equivalent established formulation, explicitly credited. The closest examined 2009/2014 edge-Roman works provide definition, inequalities or scalar results; the 2021 original Roman-polynomial work computes other graph classes; the 2022 Roman Census examines inclusion-minimal functions; and the 2023 finite atlas covers no T_n with n>=5. No inspected published theorem or publicly indexed record directly implies the infinite all-weight statement, although aliases and unindexed material present residual risks.
residual_risks: An unindexed older paper may enumerate all edge Roman dominating functions on complete graphs K_n under different terminology.
Some published primary works may contain undocumented appendix specializations outside the inspected portions; inaccessible or unindexed items have not been represented as fully cleared.

Existing general combinatorial formulas for Roman polynomial could in principle imply a support-sum representation; the specific no-isolates coefficient formula and parity census are compared as the asserted concrete result, not as an independent abstract enumeration principle.

value.rationale: The exact all-weight Roman domination polynomial on the natural infinite Johnson family J(n,2) counts every feasible ternary defense configuration, not only optimal cost, with explicit \(O(n^4)\) binomial-summand representation. The edge-support/no-isolated-vertices bijection makes the enumeration structural and yields a sharp parity split in every optimum, including exact labeled counts. This supplies an exact natural invariant and complete optimum census for a previously unenumerated infinite family, not an arbitrary finite slice, textbook substitution, or known-table recomputation. The result asserts no unproved downstream consequences.
